text:
jess-customer: Hey team — hitting you from ACME Inc. Since ~15:40 UTC our API calls to api.redwood.com/chat are getting auth errors (401) and 5xxs, latency spikes to ~900ms, and our usage spiked because our client retried. We expect traffic to stay in us‑west but traces show X-Served-Region: eu-west-1. Can you help?

alice: Thanks Jess — escalating. Can you paste a sample request/response (headers) + one trace id? Also which API key (masked) was used?

jess-customer: Sample below. Key: sk-****-acme. Trace: 01H8A2K9X0WQ3. CURL we ran: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-***-acme" -H "X-Region: us-west-2" https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat`

jess-customer (paste):
HTTP/2 503
content-type: application/json
x-served-region: eu-west-1
x-request-id: 01H8A2K9X0WQ3
server: redwood-gateway
{ "error": "service_unavailable" }

alice: Noted. @ben can you take oncall? Looks like wrong-region routing + fallback loop + auth noise.

ben: Looking. Quick hypothesis: regional healthcheck or probe suppression in us-west triggered fallback to eu-west; requests then hit a different auth shard and return 401/503 intermittently. Can you attach the customer-visible trace from our tracing UI? Also checking recent deploys.

deploy-bot: [deploy] canary rollout "model-serving/us-west" started by carla at 2025-06-03T15:39:10Z (canary 1/5).

carla: This lines up — a small canary started at 15:39 and there were a few worker restarts during warmup. If the healthcheck path `/healthz` returned 503 during warmup, the smart-router may have flipped traffic. We have a probe-suppression TTL that can hold failover for a long window if suppression is triggered.

eli: I pulled heartbeats for us-west between 15:36–15:46 UTC: shows a flapping sequence — `healthz` 200 -> 503 -> 503 -> 200, with probe suppression flag set at 15:40:22 for 300s. Router logs show: `route decision: prefer eu-west (fallback) because region us-west suppressed=true suppression_ttl=300s`.

eli (paste logs):
[2025-06-03T15:40:19Z] healthcheck /healthz -> 200
[2025-06-03T15:40:21Z] healthcheck /healthz -> 503 (worker OOM during canary boot)
[2025-06-03T15:40:22Z] probe-suppression: set=true reason=consecutive-failures ttl=300
[2025-06-03T15:40:23Z] router: fallback-to-region eu-west-1 for selector default
[2025-06-03T15:40:27Z] request 01H8A2K9X0WQ3 served-by eu-west-1 status=503

carla: That `ttl=300` is what worries me — it's a conservative default for older autoscaling events but causes long cross-region stickiness. We should avoid long suppression for canary windows.

dana: Customer asks for ETA to get them back pinned to us-west. They see billing impact from retries.

ben: Immediate mitigation options: 1) reduce probe-suppression TTL for us-west to 30s (config override), 2) add an account-level routing override to force acme-inc -> us-west until we clear the canary, 3) clear sticky LB sessions for acme-inc. Which one do we want now?

carla: Do 2 + 1. Account override is safest short-term so no more cross-region auth mismatches. TTL rollback to 30s to prevent long failovers if workers flap again. I'll prepare the route override patch and a CLI snippet.

carla (snippet):
```
redwood routes set --account acme-inc --region us-west-2 --force-override "temporary-emergency"
redwood config update probe-suppression.us-west ttl=30 --reason "emergency fix for canary-induced routing"
```

eli: I'll run healthcheck remediation: drain and restart the worker that OOMed, then flush probe suppression state for us-west. Steps:
1) `kubectl -n serving rollout restart deploy/model-worker-us-west-42`
2) `curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood.com/debug/flush-probe?region=us-west-2`
3) clear LB stickiness cookie for acme-inc via Fastly API (or clear session on our edge).

ben: ETA?

eli: Restart started 15:53 UTC, expecting workers healthy by 15:57–16:00. Flushing suppression once health is green; route override deploy ~2–3 mins.

dana: Communicated ETA to Jess. She replied: "Thanks — please ping when done, we had 27 failed calls and retries fired automatically."

ben: After remediation we'll run a quick postmortem: root cause is canary worker OOM causing transient /healthz 503 -> probe suppression TTL too long -> automatic fallback to eu-west -> customer-level auth shard mismatch -> 401s and billing from retries.

carla: Action items: 1) lower default probe-suppression TTL for canary cohorts to 30s (prod change), 2) add a cooldown so route fallback doesn't change region until X successful healthchecks, 3) improve alerting to correlate canary deploys with heartbeat flaps.

dana: Thanks everyone, I'll follow up with the customer when the override is in place. :thumbsup:

jess-customer: Confirmed they see traffic back to us-west and latency normalized ~60ms. Will monitor for 1h and report if they see issues.

ben: Closing loop — will open a short incident doc with repro steps and action items.

alice: Thanks team — marking as escalated -> eng-platform + eng-sre.
